useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

In Connect X (Connect Four), the center column is the most strategically significant column on the board. This is because a piece in the middle column can be part of many more potential four-in-a-row combinations—horizontal, vertical, and diagonal—compared to any other column. 

Player 1 (x) has opened the game by playing in Column 3 (the center column). As Player 2 (o), it is optimal to contest the center immediately. Playing in Column 3 is a strong, balanced response that:
1.  Contests the most valuable vertical space on the board.
2.  Blocks Player 1 from building an early vertical threat in the center.
3.  Positions a piece in a key location for both future offensive connections and defensive blocks.

According to theoretical analysis and standard opening strategies, Column 3 is a solid and standard response to a center-column opening, ensuring that Player 2 maintains as much control over the middle of the board as possible.
